# Independently authored stored-ZIP fixtures

108 .bin files and fixtures.json are byte-for-byte copies of the reviewed
2026-10-13 contract preparation, whose contract SHA-256 is
42a0dd539d8ccf158b94d3f3d8530f8e4716880cf087a7a05d5127aaa72db4d1.
Manifest SHA-256 is
040878bfb0204059f69562ae4c4cf8b1f4d71689525759014db104362e1f53a1.
Each file has an exact length/digest and authored layout/ordinal/outcome.
Symbolic usize_max resolves to the target's usize::MAX, including expected
ordinal fields; no u64 truncation. Mutated/truncated nominal layout ranges are
not assertions of physical validity.

cases.rs transcribes those frozen outcomes into Rust literals without a new
manifest-parser dependency. Digests, payload byte/range/CRC values, prerequisite
versus selected-operation stage and exact error fields are independently frozen,
not generated by the Rust reader. SHA256 uses the existing approved sha2 solely
to verify fixtures and construct the immutable VerifiedArtifact boundary.

CRC_SINGLETONS and CRC_LENGTHS were computed independently with Python stdlib
binascii.crc32 (source/data authoring only), after empty=0 and123456789=cbf43926
checks. CRC_LENGTHS uses byte i=(i*37+11)%256. Separate constants cover8MiB zero
bytes and the Debug sentinel [217,218,219,220]. No compiler/JVM/archive tool or
ktlsp parser generated layouts or expected results. No third-party fixture bytes
or implementation source were copied.

The preparation packet contains authoring source, independent review probes,
initial findings/fixes and exact review hashes. See ZIP_STORED.md and
ZIP_STORED_REVIEW.md for policies/current evidence. These synthetic byte layouts
are not genuine stored classfiles or proof of whole ZIP/JAR validity. Existing
pinned CommonsLang and Guava artifacts contain no stored classes; no repacking
was used to manufacture genuine archive coverage.

Current local evidence is formatting/compile-only Clippy; native runtime tests
are held for the original hosted CI under root's later grant. No runtime pass,
decompression/extraction, authenticity, JAR/semantic or parity claim follows.
